historical_references.reference: Lydiana was a name given to a 7th-century AD Visigothic queen who ruled the Kingdom of Toledo in Spain.
historical_references.context: During this time, the Visigoths were the predominant group in the region, and Lydiana's rule signified the political and religious influence of the Christianized Visigothic dynasty in the Iberian Peninsula.

historical_references.reference: Another Lydiana existed during the Roman Empire, around the 3rd century AD. This Lydiana was a renowned martyr who was venerated for her devotion to Christianity during a time when the religion was persecuted.
historical_references.context: Christianity was a minority religion during the Roman Empire, and the persecution of Christians was a common occurrence. Lydiana's martyrdom served as an inspiration to many and contributed to the spread of Christianity in the Roman Empire.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Lydiana is of European origin and has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts. Lastly, in the world of role-playing games, Lydiana is a common name for player-created characters in Tabletop Simulator and World of Warcraft, reflecting its historical and fantastical appeal.
